A.notes: A has a coherent quiet idea: warm paper, brick tones, a highlighted “light,” and simple plans/images make the studio’s identity legible. Typography is the strongest asset, but the project imagery stays quite abstract and the scroll-strip shows little beyond straightforward scrolling, so motion does not add much to the story. Craft and accessibility look solid across checks and the reduced-motion version preserves content.

B.notes: B carries one clear concept more fully: brick, light and courtyard are built into the hero arch, the project illustrations, the plans, and the section sequencing. The scroll-strip suggests purposeful section-to-section progression and process-state changes, but not enough evidence of especially rich motion; the reduced-motion fallback appears intact. Desktop feels strong, though the phone capture shows awkward long gaps/uneven project flow, which pulls craft down.

raw.why: B expresses the brief’s signature more vividly and consistently, with stronger project imagery and a more distinctive overall identity despite weaker mobile craft.
